# rev4 power-loss and thermal check (generated by losses.py)

Analytical per-period model, IKP08N65F5 data as transcribed in rev3/sim/swmodel.py (datasheet Rev 2.1; not re-fetched). 50 kHz, hard switched, synchronous CCM, dead time 200 ns, L = 2 mH, gate 15 ohm on (16.5 ohm loop), high side 11 V / low side 12 V. See the module docstring for every model term. **Estimates:** diode RthJC 3.5 K/W, the Steinmetz fit of the Fe-Si-Al core, the toroid's convection, the 100 uH DCR, the bleeders (220 kohm as rev3), and the whole low-current switching-energy model (no datasheet data below 2 A).

## 1. Cross-check against rev3 M15 (3 mH, 420 V, Tj 125 C, ngspice)

| M15 case | i at HS turn-on (A) | this model HS total / cond (W) | Qrr linear (W) | datasheet-curve Eon (W) | M15 sim total / cond (W) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A 400 V / 0.70 A | +0.64 | 3.26 / 0.75 | 3.73 | 2.87 | 3.54 / 0.61 |
| C 400 V / 0.30 A | +0.24 | 1.87 / 0.29 | 2.76 | 1.78 | 1.57 / 0.20 |
| L 390 V / 0.18 A | +0.09 | 1.26 / 0.16 | 2.47 | 1.45 | 1.10 / 0.10 |
| F 200 V / 0.35 A | +0.00 | 0.92 / 0.18 | 2.64 | 1.59 | 0.66 / 0.12 |

The baseline reproduces M15 at full load (-8 %) and is 15-40 % above it at the light-load points (where the turn-on current is near zero and the Qrr extrapolation and the Qoss / passive-floor terms dominate), so it is on the safe side there. The datasheet-curve column (Eon 20 + 20 uJ/A, no Qrr collapse at low current) is pessimistic at light load and optimistic at full load; the Qrr-linear column is the upper bound.

Model B (class-B: extra current proportional to amplitude): idle + 0.4 A x sqrt(1/6) x 0.85 = **0.439 A**; screen 0.03 A idle + 0.15 A x 0.35 = **0.082 A**. The core loss is set by the ripple flux, largest near D 0.5 (150-300 V); with mu 60 (more turns) dB falls by sqrt(60/90) and the core loss by about 1/1.5, with mu 125 it rises about 1.4x. At 400 V it is small.

The low-side shunt carries the inductor current only in the off-interval (short at 400 V). The peak shunt case is a sustained ramp-down or a short; 50 mohm at 3 A (trip) is 0.45 W: a 1 W 1225 / 2512 part is enough.

## 7. Gate drive on the link's +12 V

| Item | +12 V current (mA) |
|---|---|
| gate charge Qg ~18 nC (0-12 V) x 50 kHz | 3.6 |
| 1 nF G-E capacitors (rev3 option) x 12 V x 50 kHz | 2.4 |
| 10 kohm G-E resistors (on ~50 % of the time) | 2.4 |
| Si8271 VDD2 quiescent, ~2 mA each (estimate) | 8.0 |
| bootstrap leakage | 0.4 |
| **total with the 1 nF caps** | **16.8** |
| total without the 1 nF caps | 14.4 |

Budget 25 mA (ICD +12 V to the HV board). Gate power per device 11 mW (+7 mW with 1 nF), dissipated in the 15 / 8 ohm resistors and the driver, not in the IGBT. The 1 nF G-E caps slow the edges a little: rev3 M15 case P put +0.09 W (+3 %) on Q201 at full load; they cost 2.4 mA of the 12 V budget.

## 8. East wall: local spreading (ESTIMATE)

2 mm Al wall (k 150 W/mK, 5052-class), heat source about a TO-220 tab (r 6 mm), spreading out to r 40 mm: R_spread = ln(r2/r1) / (2 pi k t) = **1.01 K/W** per device. With the sustained worst case (QH1 ~3 W, the other three ~1.2 W, pitch ~20-25 mm) the wall under QH1 sits roughly 4 K above the wall a few cm away. So 'wall 85 C' at the device means the wall away from the devices at about 80 C. The whole wall has to take ~4-5 W (devices) into the chassis; that is the number for the chassis's own thermal budget.
